component.name: Kalendar
component.summary: A simple calendar that works with online accounts

description.p: Kalendar shows what is on by month, week or day, and keeps events in step with online calendars: Google Calendar, and any service that offers CalDAV, such as Nextcloud, iCloud and Fastmail.
Events can be added and changed without a network connection; they are sent on when there is one again.
Installed as a Flatpak, Kalendar draws the icons of the icon theme that Plasma's global theme sets. Before, it drew Breeze's icons unless the icon theme had been chosen on its own.

Installed as a Flatpak, Kalendar follows the colors of the desktop when they change while it runs, such as on a switch between a light and a dark theme. Before, parts of the window kept the old colors until Kalendar was started again.
The small month stays in place in the sidebar: only the list of calendars scrolls when the window is too low to show all of them.
The sidebar is tidier and tells more:

ul.li: The calendars of an account can be folded away with a click on its name, and each account has a small icon that says what kind it is
The small month marks the days that have events with a dot
A right click on a day of the small month offers to make an event on it
The menu of a right click closes when the title bar or another window is clicked

description.p: The agenda is the view Kalendar opens with, and shows a day at a glance:

ul.li: The agenda lists the next three or seven days one below the other, each with its events stacked beside it, so that an event late in the evening is seen without scrolling
The arrows in the toolbar go to the days before and after those the agenda shows
The view of one day is gone; the agenda takes its place
A right click on the calendar offers to make an event there, in every view

description.p: Calendar files can be imported, and the calendar of Plasma’s clock opens without a delay:

ul.li: Calendar files (.ics) are imported from the menu, by dropping them on the window, or by opening them from the file manager; a dialog shows what they hold and asks which calendar the events go to
Kalendar can be chosen as the system’s calendar application, which the Add button of Plasma’s clock opens
Kalendar runs only once: starting it again brings its window to the front
The plugin for the calendar of Plasma’s clock no longer makes the calendar open with a delay. If you installed the plugin, start Kalendar once after updating: that replaces it

description.p: The plugin for the calendar of Plasma’s clock no longer freezes the panel and the desktop once it is switched on. If you installed the plugin, start Kalendar once after updating: that replaces it.
Google calendars now come from the Google accounts of the system’s Online Accounts, and a lot was added around them:

ul.li: An agenda view of the next three or seven days
A click on an event shows it to read, with notes written as HTML shown as such; editing is one step further
Settings: accounts, 12 or 24 hours, the first day of the week, week numbers in the sidebar
The plugin for the calendar of Plasma’s clock can be installed from the settings
The sidebar can be put away, and shows when events are being fetched
Fetching events is several times faster

description.p: The first version: month, week and day views, and calendars from Google and from any service that offers CalDAV.
